newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italians, other foreigners evacuated from Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italians, other foreigners evacuated from Albania.

text.p: Around 100 Italians and other foreign nationals were evacuated from Tirana on Friday in an early morning operation by Italian military helicopters, Italian sources said.
Two huge army Chinook helicopters and four smaller navy HH-DD choppers for protection swept over Tirana and landed in the capital's main football stadium.

An Italian foreign ministry spokesman said in Rome Italy had completed an evacuation begun on Thursday, in which a total of some 1,000 Italians, other foreigners and a small number of Albanians have been taken out of the country by air and sea.
There was an uneasy calm in the streets of Tirana early on Friday, where law and order has broken down following the wholesale looting of arms depots and food warehouses by civilians.

The United States has also evacuated some of its citizens. In London the British foreign office said it had evacuated 131 people successfully from Albania on Friday morning and they were now on their way to the Italian Adriatic Sea port of Brindisi.

A foreign office spokesman said the 131, including 65 Britons, three Irish citizens, 11 Commonwealth citizens and 52 others, had been safely taken off the beach in the port of Durres about 30 km (20 miles) west of Tirana.
The group was aboard an Italian naval vessel, he said.

The evacuees were forced to spend the night on the beach after the Italian navy halted the evacuation on Thursday evening because of the chaotic situation in Durres, with armed civilians shooting wildly.
At least 10 more Britons spent Thursday night at the British embassy in the Albanian capital.

Diplomats were waiting to see how many more responded to an appeal broadcast on BBC World Service radio for British citizens to present themselves at the embassy before arranging another evacuation effort, the spokesman said.
No decision had been made on the evacuation route.
A further group of around 100 from several countries, including Germany, Austria and Greece, were gathered at the Austrian embassy in Tirana waiting for transport to take them to Durres.
Albanian authorities, buoyed by a new all-party government, have appealed unsuccessfully for calm against a campaign by rebels demanding the resignation of President Sali Berisha.

But as the country drifted towards anarchy, tanks appeared on the streets of Tirana late on Thursday and residents braced for a rampage by mobs brandishing weapons stolen from army depots -- the scene in other Albanian towns and cities.
